- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is trending down, model tends to underestimate — correct by adding 1–2% to forecasted values.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 2–4 periods.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 forecasted values.
- If forecasted mean is significantly below recent 18-day average, apply a “mean reversion” bias: adjust forecast to align with 18-day moving average within ±1.5%.
- When sentiment is rising and forecast is flat, model underreacts — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 periods.
